clue.text: Eastern city state reduced army

parts.note: CAL is an abbreviation for California, a US state
to reduce something is to cut it
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A news line about an eastern city-state cutting the size of its armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs 'city state' together as one idea; split it, so 'Eastern city' is the definition and 'state' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Calcutta (now Kolkata) is a major city in eastern India.

clue.text: Albert's withdrawn from an offer of marriage, by the way

parts.note: AN shortened to A, the indefinite article

indicators.note: something withdrawn from a word is taken out of it, so these letters are removed

parts.note: an offer of marriage is a proposal
Al is the usual short form of the name Albert

explanation.surface: Albert takes back his marriage proposal, mentioned in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove AL from A PROPOSAL and APROPOS is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos is used to introduce a remark incidentally, much as 'incidentally' itself is.

clue.text: One wouldn't turn to her page of the magazine

definitions.text: One wouldn't turn to her page of the magazine

parts.words: One wouldn't turn to her page of the magazine
parts.note: you need not turn any pages to find her: she is on the front of the magazine, not inside it

explanation.surface: A reader who never bothers looking at one woman's page in a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: The model on a magazine's front is on the outside, so no reader turns pages to reach her.

clue.text: Somewhat flat, undramatic Arctic landscape

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A description of a flat, unexciting stretch of frozen northern land.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the treeless, frozen plain found in Arctic regions.

clue.text: They take responsibility for their own lives

definitions.text: They take responsibility for their own lives

parts.words: They take responsibility for their own lives
parts.note: reads as people who own up to how they live, but 'lives' here means written life stories that the writers tell about themselves

explanation.surface: Praise for self-reliant people who answer for how they live.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of their own life stories are responsible for those accounts of their lives.

clue.text: Pub has mostly dry white wine — but this one's sweet

definitions.text: white wine — but this one's sweet

parts.note: a pub is a bar

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter, keeping most of it

parts.note: sack is an old name for a dry white wine from Spain

explanation.surface: A pub serves a dry white wine, with a contrasting sweet one noted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry white wine' looks like one phrase, but 'dry' alone gives SACK, and 'white wine' is the start of the definition, corrected by 'but this one's sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white dessert wine from Bordeaux, so it is a white wine, unlike sack, a sweet one.

clue.text: Composer's part written up for qualified academic

parts.note: Bach is the composer, and 's joins him to what follows

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means the letters are read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: A composer's piece is written up for a university scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor is a graduate holding a first university degree, so academically qualified.

clue.text: Poor artist finally famous for blurred technique

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so the letters are put into a new order
finally picks the last letter of the word artist

explanation.surface: A struggling painter finally becomes famous for a hazy style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes T from 'artist'; add FAMOUS and 'Poor' says rearrange the lot to get SFUMATO.
explanation.definitionFit: Sfumato is the painting method of softening outlines with gradual, smoky tonal shading, as Leonardo used.

clue.text: Painter allowed to show miraculous scene first

indicators.note: first says this piece goes at the front, ahead of the others

parts.note: Cana was where, in the Gospel, water was turned into wine at a wedding
to be allowed is to be let
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter is permitted to depict a miracle scene before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: Cana in Galilee is the site of Jesus's first miracle.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaletto was an 18th-century Venetian artist famous for his views of Venice.

clue.text: Frightened in underground chamber, runs some way forward

indicators.note: says one letter shifts nearer the front of the word rather than staying put

parts.note: a cavern is a large cave underground
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone scared in a cave runs a little way ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: In CAVERN, move R forward two places to get CRAVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Craven means cowardly, lacking courage.

clue.text: After whip-round, I go quiet

indicators.note: round means the word turns about and is read backwards

parts.note: a cat is a whip, as in cat-o'-nine-tails
a go or a try in a game is a turn

explanation.surface: After an office collection for a gift, someone falls silent.
explanation.walkthrough: A whip-round is a British office collection of money for a gift; 'round' is the reversal signal, read backwards on the whip.
explanation.definitionFit: Taciturn means reserved and saying little.

clue.text: Pork dish made available for woman, initially

parts.note: something spare is free or available
in Genesis, Eve was first made from Adam's rib

explanation.surface: A pork dish is set aside for a woman at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letter signal but describes what woman was at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare ribs are cuts of pork ribs, usually barbecued or roasted.

clue.text: Provide backing for family to retain heart of estate?

definitions.text: Provide backing for family to retain heart of estate?

indicators.note: retaining something holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other
backing means the word is read in reverse, from back to front

parts.note: a family line is a lineage

indicators.note: heart of picks the middle letters of the word estate

explanation.surface: Support for a family's efforts to keep the core of their property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the family word and 'to retain' wraps it round the heart of 'estate'. The whole clue also defines: an entail keeps an estate within the family line.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail land is to settle it on a line of heirs so the family keeps it.

clue.text: Like a film of jelly

parts.note: like means as
a pic is a film or picture

explanation.surface: A thin layer of jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock.

clue.text: Military instrument I dropped in battle's warmth

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a battle is an action

indicators.note: dropped means a letter falls away and is removed

parts.note: a fife is a small flute played in military bands
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier drops a band instrument amid the fervour of combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' takes the letter I out of the instrument, and 'in' puts what is left inside the battle word; the 's of 'battle's' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Affection is fondness, a feeling of warmth towards someone.

clue.text: Launch, manipulating bottom oar

indicators.note: manipulating means working something by hand, so the letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting a boat going by handling the oar at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch is a large motor-driven pleasure boat.

clue.text: Stranded abroad, initial security needed for an advance?

definitions.text: Stranded abroad, initial security needed for an advance?

parts.words: Stranded abroad, initial security needed for an advance?
parts.note: troops landed on a foreign shore need a first foothold there, held securely, before they can push inland

explanation.surface: Someone stuck overseas needs a first deposit before getting a loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advance' suggests a loan and 'security' a deposit, but both are military: an advance inland and a secured foothold on the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: A beachhead is the defended position landing troops seize on an enemy coast before advancing.

clue.text: Making piles of corn is dreadful

definitions.meaning: to shock corn is to stand sheaves together in stooks in the field

explanation.surface: Stacking up the harvest is said to be terrible work.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock is a stook of sheaves, and shocking also means appalling.

clue.text: Fail to describe why winter's early in America?

definitions.meaning: to not reach a target or standard

definitions.text: to describe why winter's early in America?
definitions.meaning: Americans call autumn the fall, and if that season is brief, winter comes sooner

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why American winters begin early.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall short is to fail to reach a target; and a short autumn, American fall, brings winter early.

clue.text: In sediment, stick some vegetables

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: lees are the sediment left in a wine barrel
gum is glue, something that makes things stick

explanation.surface: Poking a stick into mud, someone finds a few vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Legumes are pod vegetables such as peas, beans and lentils.

clue.text: Silent film star in famous family

definitions.text: Silent film star in famous family

parts.words: Silent film star in famous family
parts.note: the Marx Brothers were a famous family of comedians, and one brother never spoke on screen

explanation.surface: A film star from a celebrated family who never spoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silent film' suggests the pre-talkie era, but this star was in sound films and simply never spoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Harpo Marx was the mute, harp-playing member of the Marx Brothers comedy team.

clue.text: Keep postal order in moneybag, being mean

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a purse is a small bag for money

explanation.surface: Advice to tuck a postal order into a purse, sounding stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like stingy, but it is the verb: to purpose is to intend. 'Keep' joins the instruction to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To purpose is an old verb meaning to intend, as to mean to do something.

clue.text: Mark the end of three months as a clubman

parts.note: M is short for mark, the old German currency
September, November and December all end with the same five letters

explanation.surface: A club member marks the close of a quarter-year.
explanation.definitionFit: A member is someone who belongs to a club.

clue.text: Drink may turn cold if taken back

indicators.note: taken back means the whole run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: may and can both express being able or permitted
a go is a turn
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A warning that a drink may go cold if returned.
explanation.walkthrough: CAN + GO + C reads CANGOC; 'taken back' reverses it to COGNAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a brandy from the Cognac region of France.

clue.text: Excess of prayer interrupted by god

indicators.note: something interrupted is broken into, so the other piece goes inside it

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request or prayer
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: Too much praying, cut short by a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an overabundance, far more than is needed.

clue.text: Still a large crowd entering a single race

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one, a single

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the mile is a classic running race
a mob is a large, unruly crowd

explanation.surface: A crowd surges onto the track during a single race, which stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like 'even so', but it means motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Immobile means not moving, completely motionless.

clue.text: Poet of the British school? French, actually

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: Is this poet from the British school? No, he's really French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French, actually' warns that the poet the wordplay builds is not British: the surrealist André Breton.
explanation.definitionFit: André Breton was a French writer and poet, founder of Surrealism.

clue.text: Doing detective work, gets a number to inform

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing on accomplices to the police

explanation.surface: A detective at work picks up a number from an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosing around means prying or investigating.

clue.text: Destroyer of documents that could make mum more embarrassed

parts.note: mum means silent, and SH is the call for silence
someone more embarrassed is redder in the face

explanation.surface: A machine destroying papers that would leave mother even more embarrassed.
explanation.definitionFit: A shredder is a machine that cuts papers into strips so they cannot be read.
